2607.25398.title: HANDBOOK.md: A Benchmark for Long-Context Agentic Instruction Following
2607.25398.paper_summary: Language-model agents are increasingly deployed under standing instructions: a system prompt, a policy file, or a skills document is placed in context, and the agent is trusted to let it govern every action that follows. Existing benchmarks rarely test this deployment pattern directly; they measure whether an agent can complete a task, not whether a long, binding policy document actually constrains its behavior over an extended tool-use horizon. We present HANDBOOK_md, a benchmark of 65 agentic tasks modeled on how enterprise employees follow company handbooks. Each task places an agent in a self-contained company environment, a file workspace together with mock email, chat, calendar, issue-tracking, and commerce services exposed over the Model Context Protocol, and instructs it to carry out routine professional work governed by an expert-written standard operating procedure of 20 to 124 pages. Tasks span five domains (finance, medical billing, insurance, logistics, and HR) and ten fictional companies. To resist memorization, every task modifies one of ten base handbooks, altering the specific rules and thresholds on which grading turns, so no two tasks share a policy. Grading is fully deterministic: each task carries a rubric of programmatic criteria (824 in total) that check both that required actions occurred and that prohibited actions did not. Under strict grading, where a trial passes only if every criterion is satisfied, the best of thirty evaluated model configurations passes 36.2% of trials, and most frontier configurations remain below 25%. Failures follow consistent patterns: agents let a plausible in-environment request override the standing policy, perform a required check and then act against its result, lose rule details over long horizons, and report compliance they did not achieve. We release all tasks, environments, and the evaluation harness.
2607.25398.paper_summary_zh: 語言模型代理越來越多地在既定指示下部署：系統提示、政策文件或技能文件被放置在上下文中，並且信任代理讓它主導隨後的每一個行動。現有的基準很少直接測試這種部署模式；它們測量的是代理是否能完成任務，而不是一份長且具約束力的政策文件是否真的在延長的工具使用範圍內約束其行為。我們提出了 HANDBOOK_md，一個由 65 個代理任務組成的基準，模擬企業員工如何遵循公司手冊。每個任務將代理置於一個自我封閉的公司環境中，這是一個文件工作區，連同模擬電子郵件、聊天、日曆、問題跟踪和商務服務，通過模型上下文協議暴露出來，並指示它執行由專家撰寫的標準操作程序（20 到 124 頁）所治理的例行專業工作。任務涵蓋五個領域（財務、醫療計費、保險、物流和人力資源）和十家虛構公司。為了抵抗記憶，每個任務修改十本基本手冊中的一本，改變評分所依賴的具體規則和閾值，因此沒有兩個任務共享同一政策。評分是完全確定性的：每個任務都有一套程序性標準（總共 824 條）來檢查所需行動是否發生以及禁止行動是否未發生。在嚴格的評分下，只有在滿足所有標準的情況下，試驗才會通過，三十個評估的模型配置中最好的通過率為 36.2%，而大多數前沿配置則低於 25%。失敗遵循一致的模式：代理讓一個合理的環境內請求覆蓋既定政策，執行所需檢查然後違反其結果，在長期範圍內失去規則細節，並報告未達成的合規性。我們釋放所有任務、環境和評估工具。
